coding.note: Claims are restricted to the abstract/introduction and deduplicated: first scaled native 1-bit release, performance parity, efficiency advantages, and open-source inference implementations. Architectural and training details described in later sections are not separately coded as introductory novelty claims. Main-table comparators are from Table 1 only. All benchmark scores are described as rerun; public evaluation toolkits do not constitute independent third-party evaluation. Data sources are named without reconstructible proportions. Inference hardware and energy estimates do not disclose training compute. No independent training-run counts or explicit renaming of prior techniques are reported.

claims.quote:
we introduce BitNet b1.58 2B4T, the first
open-source, native 1-bit LLM trained at scale.
claims.claim: First open-source native 1-bit LLM trained at scale, with 2 billion parameters and 4 trillion training tokens.

claims.quote:
The core contribution of this work is to demonstrate
that a native 1-bit LLM, when trained effectively at scale, can achieve performance comparable
to leading open-weight, full-precision models of similar size across a wide range of tasks.
claims.claim: Demonstrate broad task-performance parity between a scaled native 1-bit LLM and similarly sized full-precision models.

claims.quote:
while offering significant advantages in computational efficiency, including sub-
stantially reduced memory footprint, energy consumption, and decoding latency.
claims.claim: Achieve substantially reduced memory footprint, energy consumption, and decoding latency.

claims.quote:
provide open-source
inference code optimized for both GPU and CPU execution, aiming to facilitate further research and
the practical deployment of highly efficient LLMs.
claims.claim: Release optimized open-source GPU and CPU inference implementations alongside the model weights.
